label: copy-phase fed-back c, esp. when next output is w/d/c (early recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the step where the fed-back input is the letter c (98% of activation mass has in_tok == c; it never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on the first occurrence of a token). Almost every copy-phase c input gets some activation (recall 0.96, mass recall 0.98), but most are tiny, so precision for in_tok==c alone is only 5%. Magnitude depends on the token being output next: it is strongest when the original token after c is w (55% of mass), then d (24%), then c (11%). It is also strongest early in the recall (recall_idx 1-3) and in short sequences (L 3-5), and weaker for later recall positions and L >= 7. Top examples are "c w w" / "c d w" patterns where w comes right after c. Weak activations also appear when w shows up a few tokens after c, and a few on fed-back w/d inputs. The predicate (copy phase, input c, output w/d/c, recall_idx <= 3) gets dev F1 0.59 and mass recall 0.75. It does not fire on c in the original phase, or on any other letters or digits apart from a little on w and d.
